set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac MRI
set1.q: What is done before a cardiovascular magnetic resonance study is ordered?
opts: A coronary angiogram
Angiography is invasive and is not a prerequisite for magnetic resonance.
A nuclear perfusion study
A perfusion study is not the stated prerequisite; an echocardiogram is done before magnetic resonance is ordered.
An echocardiogram
Correct. It is the first-line functional study, and magnetic resonance answers what it leaves unresolved rather than replacing it.
A coronary calcium score
Calcium scoring is not the stated prerequisite; an echocardiogram is done first.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 56

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
set1.q: What can be done during a coronary angiogram that cannot be done during any of the noninvasive studies?
opts: Treatment, by percutaneous coronary intervention there and then
Correct. It is the one study that can fix what it finds while the catheter is still in place.
Measurement of ejection fraction
Ejection fraction can be obtained noninvasively by echocardiography.
Assessment of myocardial viability
Viability is assessed noninvasively by nuclear imaging or magnetic resonance.
Calcium scoring
Calcium scoring is a noninvasive computed tomography study and needs no catheter.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 72

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set1.q: Which patient factors, other than oesophageal disease, contraindicate a transoesophageal study?
opts: An uncooperative patient, restricted neck movement, airway risk

Correct. Two are about whether the patient can be positioned and kept still, and one is about whether the airway can be protected under sedation. In full: altered mental status or an uncooperative patient, cervical spine arthritis with reduced range of motion, and obstructive sleep apnoea or other risk of airway compromise.
Significant renal impairment
Renal impairment matters for iodinated contrast rather than for this study.
An implanted cardiac pacemaker
A pacemaker is not among the listed contraindications for this study.
Atrial fibrillation
Atrial fibrillation is a reason to look for appendage thrombus rather than a contraindication.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 26

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of nuclear cardiology studies
set1.q: Tracer uptake in a region is normal at rest but reduced after stress. What does that pattern indicate?
opts: Infarcted, non-viable tissue
Infarcted tissue shows no uptake in either set. Reduced uptake only after stress indicates inducible ischaemia.
Inducible ischaemia, from a coronary stenosis
Correct. The tissue is alive but cannot increase its supply when demand rises, which is what a stenosis does.
Normal myocardium
Normal tissue maintains or increases uptake under stress rather than losing it.
A pericardial effusion
Pericardial fluid is not assessed by perfusion imaging; the pattern described indicates inducible ischaemia.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 48

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
set1.q: What does RIGHT heart catheterisation assess?
opts: The coronary artery anatomy
Coronary anatomy is assessed from the left side rather than the right.
Right-sided pressures, pulmonary resistance, valves and shunts

Correct. The pulmonary side of the circulation, and the shunts that connect the two sides. In full: right atrial and right ventricular pressure, pulmonary artery and occlusion pressure, pulmonary vascular resistance, tricuspid and pulmonic valve function, and intracardiac shunts.
Aortic and mitral valve function
Both are left heart structures, assessed at left rather than right catheterisation.
Systemic vascular resistance
That is a left heart measurement; the right study gives pulmonary vascular resistance instead.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 69

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set1.q: How does an exercise stress test detect myocardial ischaemia?
opts: Directly, by imaging myocardial perfusion during exercise
Direct perfusion imaging is what the nuclear study adds; the standard exercise test relies on the electrocardiogram.
By measuring coronary artery calcium before and after exercise
Calcium scoring is a non-contrast computed tomography study and is not part of stress testing.
Indirectly, by continuous electrocardiographic monitoring
Correct. It never images the heart at all; it infers ischaemia from what the electrocardiogram does as demand rises, which is why the word is indirectly.
By measuring ejection fraction at peak exercise
Ejection fraction is an echocardiographic measure; the standard exercise test does not obtain it.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 29

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of nuclear cardiology studies
set1.q: A region of myocardium shows no tracer uptake on either the stress or the rest images. What does that indicate?
opts: Dead tissue
Correct. Uptake requires functional myocardium, so tissue that never lights up is not ischaemic but infarcted.
Inducible ischaemia
Inducible ischaemia shows reduced uptake after stress with better uptake at rest, rather than absent uptake in both.
Normal myocardium
Normal tissue takes up tracer in both sets of images; absent uptake in both indicates infarction.
An artefact of the gamma camera
Absent uptake in both sets is a finding rather than an artefact.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 48

set1.io: Compare and contrast cardiovascular imaging modalities
set1.q: What is the standing of chest radiography in cardiac evaluation?
opts: It is not the primary modality, but it gives useful clues when obtained
Correct. It is rarely the study you order to answer a cardiac question, and frequently the study you already have, which is why reading it well matters.
It is the primary modality for assessing cardiac function
Function and detailed cardiac anatomy are exactly what it does not assess.
It has no role in cardiac assessment
It visualises the cardiac silhouette, the great vessels and the pulmonary vasculature, all of which carry cardiac information.
It replaces echocardiography when the patient cannot lie flat
It does not substitute for echocardiography; the two answer different questions.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 4

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set1.q: Which exercise modalities are used, and which is preferred among the cycles?
opts: Treadmill only
Cycle ergometry is described alongside the treadmill as one of the two common modalities.
Arm ergometry, as first choice
Arm ergometry is listed but the stationary bicycle is the preferred cycle.
Step testing
Step testing is not among the modalities described, which are the treadmill, the cycle ergometer and arm ergometry.
Treadmill and cycle ergometer
Correct, and arm ergometry exists for patients who cannot use their legs, which keeps the test available to more people. With the stationary bicycle preferred.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 30

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set1.q: Which complications of exercise stress testing are described?
opts: Contrast-induced nephropathy
No contrast is given in a standard exercise stress test. The complications are arrhythmia, angina, infarction and death.
Arrhythmia, angina, infarction and death
Correct. The test deliberately provokes the thing it is looking for, which is why it is supervised and why it has a stopping rule.
Malignancy induced by radiation exposure
The standard exercise test uses no ionising radiation. Its complications are arrhythmia, angina, infarction and death.
Oesophageal perforation
That risk belongs to transoesophageal echocardiography rather than to exercise testing.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 30

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of nuclear cardiology studies
set1.q: On what principle does radionuclide myocardial perfusion imaging work?
opts: Diseased myocardium takes up more tracer than normal myocardium
Uptake is reduced rather than increased where flow is reduced.
Tracer is taken up only by scarred tissue
Uptake marks functional, viable tissue; scar does not take it up.
The tracer is metabolised into a contrast agent within the coronary arteries
The tracer emits gamma rays that the camera detects rather than becoming contrast.
Under stress, diseased myocardium receives less blood flow than normal myocardium
Correct, so comparing stress images against rest images is what makes the difference visible rather than either set alone.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 49

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac MRI
set1.q: What does cardiovascular magnetic resonance avoid that computed tomography does not?
opts: Dependence on the operator
Operator dependence is a limitation of ultrasound rather than the point of comparison here.
Any need for a resting heart rate
Rate control is a computed tomography requirement; it is not what magnetic resonance is described as avoiding.
Both ionising radiation and iodinated contrast
Correct. Both avoided at once, which matters most in the young patient and in the patient with impaired kidneys.
Sedation and airway monitoring
Sedation is required for transoesophageal echocardiography rather than being the contrast drawn here.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 55

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set1.q: A patient stops an exercise stress test having reached 70 per cent of their predicted maximum heart rate, with no electrocardiographic changes. How should the result be read?
opts: A negative test, excluding ischaemia
A negative result only counts once the heart rate threshold has been reached.
A positive test
Nothing here indicates ischaemia; the problem is that the test was not taken far enough to say.
Inadequate to exclude ischaemia
Correct. The threshold for a valid test is 85 per cent, so a negative result below it says nothing about the heart, only about the test.
Equivocal, requiring repeat in six months
The result is uninterpretable rather than equivocal, and the stated consequence is that ischaemia has not been excluded.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 31

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set1.q: Which types of stress test are described?
opts: Exercise, pharmacological, treadmill and bicycle
Echocardiographic and nuclear stress testing are described as separate types alongside these two.
Nuclear, magnetic resonance, catheter and Doppler
Magnetic resonance is described separately from the stress tests rather than as one of them.
Treadmill, bicycle, handgrip and cold pressor
These are two modalities within the standard exercise test rather than two types of stress test.
Exercise, echocardiographic, nuclear, pharmacological
Correct. Two axes run through the list: how the heart is stressed, and how it is then imaged, and the four names are combinations of those two. Echocardiographic, nuclear and pharmacological.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 28

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set1.q: What is obtained before an exercise stress test begins?
opts: A resting echocardiogram in every case
A resting echocardiogram is obtained for the echocardiographic stress test rather than for the standard one.
A coronary calcium score
Calcium scoring is a separate computed tomography study. What is obtained first is a resting tracing and blood pressure.
A resting electrocardiogram
Correct. Without the resting baseline there is nothing to compare the exercise tracing against. Blood pressure both supine and standing.
A radionuclide injection at rest
Resting tracer injection belongs to the nuclear perfusion study.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 33

set1.io: Identify common abnormal cardiovascular imaging findings
set1.q: Which structures can be at least partly seen on a chest radiograph for cardiac purposes?
opts: The coronary arteries and the cardiac valves
Neither is visualised on a plain radiograph; calcification of a valve may be seen, but not the valve's structure.
The cardiac conduction system
Conduction is assessed electrically rather than radiographically.
The pericardial fluid volume
Pericardial calcification may be visible, but fluid volume is not measured on a plain film.
Cardiac silhouette, great vessels, lungs and pleura
Correct, along with the pulmonary vasculature. Note what is absent: the chambers, the valves and the coronary arteries are not among them.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 4

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set1.q: Which patients receive a pharmacological rather than an exercise stress test?
opts: Those with a normal resting electrocardiogram
A normal resting tracing makes the standard exercise test easier to interpret rather than ruling it out.
Those with renal impairment
Renal impairment is a consideration for iodinated contrast rather than for exercise capacity.
Those who cannot exercise
Correct. The heart still has to be stressed; if the legs cannot do it, a drug does it instead. Usually because of a physical limitation.
Those under forty years of age
Age is not the basis for choosing it; inability to exercise, usually from a physical limitation, is.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 38

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac CT
set1.q: What advantages does cardiac computed tomography have over echocardiography?
opts: Assessment of cardiac function as well as anatomy
Function is exactly what it cannot assess; that is left to echocardiography and magnetic resonance.
Superior resolution and noninvasive coronary assessment
Correct, with fast acquisition and interpretation as well, which together make it the anatomical study of choice. It also shows internal structures directly, and acquires and reports quickly.
Freedom from ionising radiation
Radiation is one of its disadvantages rather than an advantage; magnetic resonance is what avoids it.
Independence from heart rate and rhythm
It is rhythm and rate dependent, which is why rate control is given beforehand.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 44

set1.io: Compare and contrast cardiovascular imaging modalities
set1.q: On a vascular ultrasound, how does tissue density relate to the image?
opts: The denser the structure the darker it appears
The relationship runs the other way: dense structures return more signal and appear lighter.
Density does not affect the image, only depth does
Both matter: depth sets position on the screen and density sets brightness.
The denser the structure the lighter it appears
Correct, and superficial structures sit nearer the top of the screen, which together let you orient any image without being told what it is. So air is black and bone is near white.
Only flowing blood produces any signal
Tissue of all kinds reflects sound; Doppler is what adds flow information.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 14

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
set1.q: What does electrophysiological testing do?
opts: Assesses myocardial perfusion under stress conditions
Perfusion under stress is the nuclear study. Electrophysiological testing investigates rhythm disorders.
Measures the cardiothoracic ratio
That is a chest radiograph measurement rather than an electrophysiological one.
Visualises coronary anatomy
Coronary anatomy is shown by angiography; electrophysiological testing locates arrhythmias.
Investigates rhythm disorders and locates an arrhythmia

Correct, and where applicable it treats as well as diagnoses, by ablating the tissue it has just located. It reveals the precise location, and where applicable treats it by ablation in the same sitting.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 61

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
set1.q: Which is a listed indication for coronary angiography?
opts: Screening an asymptomatic patient
Screening is not an indication for an invasive study carrying the risks this one does.
Severe angina despite medical therapy

Correct, together with acute infarction, a high-risk noninvasive test result, high-risk patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery, and arrhythmias suspected to be vascular in origin. Or unstable angina.
Suspected deep venous thrombosis
That is assessed by vascular ultrasound rather than by coronary angiography.
Newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation alone
Atrial fibrillation alone is not among the listed indications.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 71

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
set1.q: What does LEFT heart catheterisation assess?
opts: Coronary anatomy, aortic pressure and left ventricular function

Correct. Everything on the systemic side of the circulation, which is the side the left heart serves. Together with systemic vascular resistance, and aortic and mitral valve function, and left ventricular pressure.
Pulmonary artery pressure and vascular resistance
These are right heart measurements. The left heart study assesses coronary anatomy and the systemic side.
Tricuspid and pulmonic valve function
These are assessed at right heart catheterisation; the left study covers the aortic and mitral valves.
Right atrial pressure
That is a right heart measurement rather than one obtained from the left side.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 68

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set1.q: Why is a transoesophageal study used in a patient presenting with cerebral ischaemia?
opts: It measures cerebral blood flow directly and noninvasively
Echocardiography images the heart rather than the cerebral circulation.
It can find thrombus in the left atrial appendage
Correct. It looks for the source rather than the consequence, and the appendage is the site the transthoracic study sees worst.
It assesses the carotid arteries
The carotids are assessed by vascular ultrasound. The transoesophageal study looks for a cardiac source of embolus.
It excludes coronary stenosis
Coronary stenosis is not assessed by echocardiography; it needs computed tomography angiography or catheter angiography.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 23

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
set1.q: Which complications of coronary angiography occur at the catheter insertion site?
opts: Contrast nephropathy and arrhythmia
Both are recognised risks of the procedure but are not site complications.
Oesophageal perforation
That belongs to transoesophageal echocardiography rather than to arterial catheterisation.
Pneumothorax
Not among the described site complications, which are haematoma and pseudoaneurysm.
Haematoma and pseudoaneurysm
Correct, and the pseudoaneurysm is the one to check for deliberately, since it maintains a continuous communication with the artery.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 78

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac CT
set1.q: What is the fundamental limitation of cardiac computed tomography compared with echocardiography and magnetic resonance?
opts: It assesses anatomy but not function
Correct. It shows the structure in great detail and cannot tell you how well it is working, which decides when it is the wrong study.
It cannot show the coronary arteries
Noninvasive coronary assessment is one of its strengths. What it cannot show is function.
It cannot be used in patients with a normal heart rate
A controlled heart rate is what it requires rather than what excludes it.
It requires an endoscope
No endoscope is involved; that belongs to transoesophageal echocardiography.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 44

set1.io: Measure the cardiothoracic ratio to evaluate cardiac enlargement
set1.q: Why does the cardiothoracic ratio require a properly performed posteroanterior film?
opts: Projection alters the apparent size of the cardiac silhouette
Correct. A ratio measured off the wrong projection is a measurement of the technique rather than of the heart.
Only a posteroanterior film shows the pulmonary vasculature
Vasculature is visible on other projections; it is the silhouette measurement that depends on projection.
Contrast is required and is only given for posteroanterior films
No contrast is involved in measuring the ratio; it is the projection that alters the apparent silhouette size.
The ratio can only be calculated with electrocardiographic gating
Gating belongs to cardiac computed tomography rather than to plain radiography.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 8

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
set1.q: What does catheter ablation do during electrophysiological testing?
opts: Stimulates the area to restore normal conduction
Stimulation is used to identify the arrhythmia; the ablation destroys rather than restores.
Inactivates part of the heart by destroying that tissue
Correct. The tissue is not merely silenced but destroyed, which is what makes the treatment definitive.
Places a permanent pacing wire in the atrium
Catheters are placed for the study, but ablation itself destroys tissue.
Delivers a drug directly to the arrhythmic focus
Ablation is a physical rather than a pharmacological treatment.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 62

set1.io: Identify common abnormal cardiovascular imaging findings
set1.q: What is cephalisation on a chest radiograph?
opts: Fluid tracking into the interlobar fissures
That would be described as effusion or fissural fluid rather than cephalisation.
The trachea deviating toward the apex
Tracheal deviation is a different sign entirely. Cephalisation is enlargement of the upper zone vessels.
Calcification of the aortic arch
Great vessel calcification is listed separately from cephalisation.
Upper zone vessels becoming larger
Correct. Flow redistributes upward, which is why the sign sits in the lungs while the problem is in the heart.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 9

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set1.q: When is an exercise stress test terminated?
opts: At maximum performance
Correct. Three separate stopping conditions, only one of which is the patient simply having had enough. On signs or symptoms of ischaemia, or at a predetermined endpoint.
Only when the patient asks to stop
The patient's request is not the only stopping condition; ischaemic signs and a predetermined endpoint also stop it.
After a fixed twelve minutes regardless of response
No fixed duration is given; the endpoints are performance, symptoms or a predetermined target.
When blood pressure returns to baseline
Blood pressure is monitored through the test rather than used as the endpoint.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 33

set1.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
set1.q: How is coronary angiography performed?
opts: Under general anaesthesia with the patient intubated
Local anaesthesia with intravenous sedation is what is described, with fluoroscopic guidance.
Under local anaesthesia with intravenous sedation

Correct, and pressures are measured as the catheter goes, so it yields haemodynamic information alongside the pictures. With catheters guided by fluoroscopy and contrast injected into each coronary artery.
Without contrast, using ultrasound guidance
Radiographic contrast is injected into each coronary artery.
Through the oesophagus
The oesophageal route belongs to transoesophageal echocardiography.
set1.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 72

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set2.q: Why is transthoracic echocardiography the most common echo procedure?
opts: It gives better detail of the posterior structures
Posterior and inferior detail is exactly where it is weaker than the transoesophageal study.
It requires no operator training
Operator dependence applies to ultrasound generally. Its advantage is being noninvasive and available at the bedside.
It can be performed at the bedside and is noninvasive
Correct. Availability rather than image quality is what makes it the default, and the trade is detail at the back of the heart.
It is the only echo that can use Doppler
Doppler is available in both studies. The transthoracic study leads because it is noninvasive and bedside-capable.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 22

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set2.q: For which patient is an echocardiographic stress test the appropriate initial choice?
opts: One who cannot exercise at all
A patient unable to exercise is given a pharmacological stress test.
One with a normal resting electrocardiogram who can exercise
That patient can have the standard exercise test, which is simpler.
One who can exercise but whose resting tracing is abnormal
Correct. The electrocardiogram cannot be read for ischaemia if it is already abnormal, so the imaging has to carry the answer instead.
One with suspected aortic dissection
Dissection is assessed by imaging the aorta rather than by stress testing.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 37

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set2.q: What does echocardiography evaluate?
opts: The coronary artery calcium score
Calcium scoring is done by non-contrast cardiac computed tomography.
The distribution of coronary atherosclerotic plaque
Plaque distribution requires computed tomography angiography or catheter angiography.
The electrical conduction pathways of the heart
Conduction is assessed by electrocardiography and electrophysiological testing.
Chamber size, ventricular function, valves, shunts and pressures

Correct. It is the functional study of the heart, which is what separates it from computed tomography, and Doppler is what adds flow and velocity to it. Wall thickness and ejection fraction come with the ventricular assessment, and Doppler adds flow and velocity.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 20

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set2.q: Which structures does a transoesophageal study show in more detail than a transthoracic one?
opts: The right ventricle and the tricuspid valve
The gain is on the posterior and inferior side of the heart rather than on the right-sided structures.
Left atrium, mitral valve, aorta and coronaries
Correct, with the pulmonary artery too. The probe sits directly behind the heart, so the structures that gain are the posterior ones.
The pericardium alone
The improvement is not confined to the pericardium; it covers the left atrium, mitral valve, pulmonary artery, aorta and coronary arteries.
The coronary calcium burden
Calcium scoring is a non-contrast computed tomography measurement rather than an echocardiographic one.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 22

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set2.q: Which of these is a stated indication for exercise stress testing?
opts: Cardiac assessment before non-cardiac surgery in a high-risk patient
Correct, alongside symptoms suggesting ischaemia, known ischaemic disease with a change in status, prior revascularisation and newly diagnosed heart failure.
Acute chest pain before acute coronary syndrome has been excluded
The indication applies specifically after acute coronary syndrome and infarction have been excluded, not before.
Suspected aortic dissection
Dissection is assessed by imaging the aorta rather than by stressing the heart.
Screening an asymptomatic patient with no risk factors
Screening in that setting is not among the listed indications.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 32

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set2.q: What distinguishes a transthoracic from a transoesophageal echocardiogram?
opts: One uses Doppler and the other does not
Both can use Doppler. What separates them is whether the transducer sits outside the body or inside it.
The transducer is outside the body in one, inside in the other
Correct, and everything else about the two -- invasiveness, sedation, contraindications, and how much posterior detail you get -- follows from that single difference.
One uses ionising radiation while the other does not
Neither uses ionising radiation. The difference is the position of the transducer, outside the body or within it.
One assesses valves and the other assesses chambers
Both assess valves and chambers; the difference is the transducer position.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 20

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set2.q: For which of these is a transoesophageal study specifically useful?
opts: Coronary artery calcium scoring
That is a non-contrast computed tomography study. The transoesophageal study excels at posterior structures.
Valve vegetations
Correct. All are small, posterior, or both, which is precisely where the transthoracic view falls short. Prosthetic valve function, cardiac tumours and left atrial appendage thrombus.
Assessing exercise capacity
Exercise capacity is assessed by stress testing rather than by an echocardiogram at rest.
Measuring the cardiothoracic ratio
That is measured on a chest radiograph rather than by echocardiography.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 23

set2.io: Compare and contrast cardiovascular imaging modalities
set2.q: Which combination of advantages does vascular ultrasound offer?
opts: Superior resolution to computed tomography with no operator dependence
Resolution is not its strength and it is highly operator dependent.
Reliable assessment of deep vessels regardless of body habitus
Deep vessels are harder to assess and body habitus is an explicit limitation.
Fast, portable, repeatable, no ionising radiation
Correct. The combination of no radiation and easy repetition is what makes it the study you can do again tomorrow without cost to the patient. It shows both anatomy and flow.
Independence from the angle at which the probe is held
Probe angle can affect measurements, which is one of its limitations.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 17

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set2.q: What does a transoesophageal study require that a transthoracic one does not?
opts: Throat anaesthesia, sedation and monitoring
Correct. It is a procedure rather than a scan, which is why it carries a contraindication list and the transthoracic study does not.
Iodinated contrast given intravenously
No iodinated contrast is used in echocardiography; the transoesophageal study needs anaesthesia, sedation and monitoring.
Electrocardiographic gating of the images
Gating belongs to cardiac computed tomography. The transoesophageal study requires sedation and airway monitoring.
A period of fasting from fluids only
The requirements described are anaesthesia, sedation and monitoring.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 25

set2.io: Identify common abnormal cardiovascular imaging findings
set2.q: Which chest radiograph findings are given as indicators of cardiac pathology?
opts: Coronary artery stenosis and the distribution of plaque
These require computed tomography angiography or catheter angiography.
Oedema, effusion, cardiomegaly, cephalisation and calcification

Correct, with tension physiology completing the list. Several are about the lungs rather than the heart, which is the point: the heart announces itself through what it does to everything around it. The calcification may be of the great vessels, the valves or the pericardium, and tension physiology completes the list.
Ejection fraction and regional wall motion abnormality
Both are functional measures requiring echocardiography or magnetic resonance.
Valve pressure gradients and regurgitant volume
These are Doppler measurements made on echocardiography rather than findings visible on a plain film.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 6

set2.io: Compare and contrast cardiovascular imaging modalities
set2.q: Which limitations are described for vascular ultrasound?
opts: Ionising radiation dose and contrast nephrotoxicity
Neither applies: ultrasound uses no ionising radiation and no iodinated contrast.
Dependence on heart rate and rhythm
Rate and rhythm dependence belongs to cardiac computed tomography.
Highly operator dependent, limited by body habitus
Correct. Calcification causes acoustic shadowing, which matters because the vessels most worth imaging are often the ones most calcified. Degraded by bone, air and calcification.
Inability to show blood flow
Showing both anatomy and flow is one of its advantages rather than a limitation, with Doppler supplying the flow.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 18

set2.io: Compare and contrast cardiovascular imaging modalities
set2.q: Why does calcification degrade a vascular ultrasound image?
opts: It causes acoustic shadowing
Correct. Sound does not pass through, so everything behind the calcium is unassessable rather than merely indistinct.
It absorbs the ionising radiation before it reaches the vessel
No ionising radiation is involved in ultrasound. Calcification blocks sound, casting an acoustic shadow behind it.
It produces a blooming artefact that exaggerates the lesion
Blooming from calcification is a computed tomography artefact.
It prevents the vein from collapsing under compression
Failure to collapse indicates thrombus rather than calcification.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 18

set2.io: Identify common abnormal cardiovascular imaging findings
set2.q: In which patients is cephalisation seen?
opts: Pneumothorax and pleural effusion
Neither is given as a cause. Cephalisation is seen in heart failure and pulmonary hypertension.
Coronary artery disease without failure
Coronary disease alone does not produce it; the sign follows raised pulmonary pressure in failure or pulmonary hypertension.
Pericardial calcification
Calcification is listed as a separate radiographic finding rather than as a form of cephalisation.
Heart failure and pulmonary hypertension
Correct. Both raise pressure in the pulmonary circulation, and the redistribution upward is the radiographic consequence.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 9

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of nuclear cardiology studies
set2.q: How is the heart stressed for a nuclear perfusion study in a patient who cannot exercise?
opts: By transoesophageal pacing
Pacing is not the described method; pharmacological stress with an agent such as adenosine is.
By cold pressor testing
Not among the described methods. Pharmacological stress, with an agent such as adenosine, is used instead.
The study cannot be performed without exercise
Pharmacological stress exists precisely so that it can be performed without exercise.
Pharmacologically, with an agent such as adenosine
Correct. The stress can be produced by exercise or by drug, and the imaging is the same either way.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 47

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set2.q: Why must a Zenker's diverticulum be identified before a transoesophageal study?
opts: It prevents adequate sedation
Sedation is not the issue; the hazard is that the probe may enter and perforate the pouch.
The probe risks entering and perforating the pouch
Correct, and because it is a pouch rather than a narrowing, the operator may feel nothing wrong until the damage is done.
It causes a false positive for vegetations
It is a procedural hazard rather than an imaging artefact: the probe risks entering and perforating the pouch.
It makes the patient unable to swallow the local anaesthetic
The concern is perforation rather than anaesthetic administration.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 26

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac CT
set2.q: Why are cardiac medications given before a cardiac computed tomography study?
opts: To dilate the coronary arteries so contrast reaches the myocardium
Rate control is the stated reason, together with electrocardiographic synchronisation.
To control heart rate, since the moving heart degrades the images
Correct, and the study is also synchronised to an electrocardiogram so the heart can be examined at chosen points in the cycle.
To prevent an allergic reaction to the contrast
Premedication for contrast allergy is not what is described here.
To provoke ischaemia during the scan
Provoking ischaemia is what a stress test does; the medication here steadies the heart.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 41

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set2.q: What is the echocardiogram looking for after exercise, and why must it be obtained quickly?
opts: Valve gradients, which take time to develop
The study looks for induced wall motion abnormality rather than valve gradients.
Pericardial fluid, which accumulates after exertion
Pericardial fluid is not what the post-exercise images are looking for.
Abnormal left ventricular wall motion induced by exercise
Correct. The finding is transient, so the patient is asked to dismount quickly and the heart is imaged before it settles. Which resolves as the heart recovers.
Coronary calcium, which is best seen at high heart rates
Calcium is assessed by computed tomography and is unrelated to heart rate.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 37

set2.io: Compare and contrast cardiovascular imaging modalities
set2.q: How does a vascular ultrasound image form?
opts: Ionising radiation is absorbed differently by tissues of differing density
That describes radiography; ultrasound uses no ionising radiation.
A magnetic field aligns protons which then emit radiofrequency signal
That describes magnetic resonance. Ultrasound works by emitting sound pulses and reading the returning echoes.
An injected tracer is taken up and emits gamma rays
That describes nuclear imaging. Ultrasound forms its image from reflected high-frequency sound.
Quartz crystals emit pulses that reflect off tissue

Correct. The returning echoes are what the machine turns into a picture, so anything that stops sound returning leaves a gap in it. The pulses are high frequency, and what returns depends on the density of what they meet.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 14

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of nuclear cardiology studies
set2.q: How does nuclear perfusion imaging compare with standard and echocardiographic stress testing?
opts: It is less accurate but faster
It is described as more accurate than standard and echocardiographic stress testing rather than less.
It is equivalent in accuracy but avoids radiation
It uses a radioactive tracer, and it is described as more accurate.
It assesses anatomy rather than perfusion
It assesses perfusion and thus viability rather than anatomy.
Its sensitivity and specificity are superior
Correct, which is why it is worth the tracer and the radiation when the simpler tests have not settled the question.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 49

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
set2.q: What is coronary angiography the gold standard for?
opts: Coronary artery anatomy and cardiac function
Correct, which is why it is usually performed before any percutaneous or surgical intervention on the coronary arteries.
Assessing myocardial viability
Viability is assessed by nuclear perfusion imaging or magnetic resonance.
Measuring the coronary calcium score
Calcium scoring is a non-contrast computed tomography study.
Detecting valve vegetations
Vegetations are sought on echocardiography. Angiography is the gold standard for coronary anatomy and cardiac function.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 66

set2.io: Compare and contrast cardiovascular imaging modalities
set2.q: Which of these is NOT among the listed indications for vascular ultrasound?
opts: Assessment of coronary artery stenosis
Correct -- this is not one. The coronary arteries are not accessible to surface vascular ultrasound; they are assessed by computed tomography angiography or catheter angiography.
Deep vein thrombosis study and vascular access
Both are listed indications, alongside carotid evaluation, aneurysm assessment and venous insufficiency.
Carotid evaluation after stroke, transient ischaemic attack or myocardial infarction
This is a listed indication, alongside deep vein thrombosis studies, vascular access and aneurysm evaluation.
Abdominal aortic aneurysm evaluation and varicose veins
Both are listed indications, alongside vascular access, deep vein thrombosis studies and carotid assessment.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 16

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac CT
set2.q: What is the blooming artefact, and why does it matter?
opts: Motion during the scan blurs the coronary arteries
Motion blur is a separate problem, addressed by rate control and gating.
Heavy calcification appears larger than it is
Correct. The artefact exaggerates the very lesion the study was ordered to assess, which is a limitation worth naming rather than a curiosity. So a stenosis looks more severe.
Contrast pools in the ventricle and obscures the valve
That is not what blooming describes. Blooming makes dense calcium appear larger than it is.
Radiation scatter degrades the image at the edges
Blooming relates to dense calcium appearing larger than it is, rather than to radiation scatter.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 44

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set2.q: In which position does a patient lie initially for transthoracic echocardiography?
opts: Supine and flat throughout
The patient starts in the left lateral decubitus position and is repositioned.
Prone
The prone position is not used. The patient starts in left lateral decubitus and is repositioned for other views.
Left lateral decubitus
Correct. It brings the heart toward the chest wall, and the patient is moved through other positions to obtain the different views.
Standing
The study is performed lying, starting in the left lateral decubitus position.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 24

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac CT
set2.q: Which is an indication for cardiac computed tomography rather than the angiographic study?
opts: Detecting and excluding coronary stenosis
Stenosis detection is the indication for the angiographic study.
Assessing exercise capacity
Exercise capacity is assessed by stress testing rather than by cardiac computed tomography.
Pre-operative planning before cardiac surgery

Correct, alongside calcium deposits, coronary anatomical anomalies and congenital disease, and it is usually done immediately before the angiographic study. Particularly valvular and great vessel procedures.
Evaluating deep venous thrombosis
Deep vein thrombosis is assessed by vascular ultrasound rather than by cardiac computed tomography.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 43

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac MRI
set2.q: Which aortic conditions is cardiovascular magnetic resonance used to diagnose and monitor?
opts: Aneurysm, dissection, haematoma, coarctation
Correct. All four are questions about the wall and the lumen of a large vessel, which is where its detailed anatomy is most useful.
The coronary artery calcium burden
Calcium is scored by non-contrast computed tomography rather than by magnetic resonance.
Valve vegetations
Vegetations are sought on echocardiography, particularly the transoesophageal study.
Deep venous thrombosis
Deep vein thrombosis is assessed by vascular ultrasound rather than by cardiovascular magnetic resonance.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 56

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac MRI
set2.q: Which cardiomyopathy questions is cardiovascular magnetic resonance used to answer?
opts: The degree of coronary stenosis
Stenosis is assessed by computed tomography angiography or catheter angiography.
Exercise capacity
Exercise capacity is assessed by stress testing rather than by magnetic resonance.
Left atrial appendage thrombus
Appendage thrombus is sought on transoesophageal echocardiography.
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Correct. Each turns on what the muscle itself is doing, which is where it outperforms the studies that show the arteries. Ischaemic against nonischaemic, acute myocarditis and cardiac sarcoidosis.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 57

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
set2.q: Which oesophageal conditions contraindicate a transoesophageal echocardiogram?
opts: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
Reflux alone is not listed. Stricture, malignancy and bleeding varices are the oesophageal contraindications.
A history of oesophageal candidiasis
Not among the listed contraindications, which are stricture, malignancy and varices with recent or active bleeding.
Recent barium swallow
Not among the listed contraindications; stricture, malignancy and bleeding varices are the oesophageal ones.
Stricture, malignancy or bleeding varices
Correct. All three mean passing a probe risks perforation or haemorrhage, which is the hazard the contraindication list exists to avoid.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 26

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
set2.q: Which electrocardiographic changes during an exercise stress test suggest ischaemia?
opts: ST elevation with reciprocal change
The changes described for this test are ST depression and ectopy rather than elevation.
ST depression
Correct. Both appear as the heart is worked and are what the continuous monitoring exists to catch. Or the development of premature ventricular contractions.
A prolonged QT interval
QT prolongation is not among the described findings; ST depression and premature ventricular contractions are.
Loss of P waves
Absent P waves indicate atrial fibrillation rather than the ischaemic changes described.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 29

set2.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac CT
set2.q: What is a non-contrast cardiac computed tomography particularly useful for?
opts: Coronary artery calcium scoring
Correct. Calcium is dense enough to be seen without contrast, so the study that needs no contrast is the one that measures it.
Assessing coronary stenosis
Assessing stenosis requires contrast, which is what computed tomography angiography adds.
Measuring ejection fraction
Ejection fraction is a functional measure obtained by echocardiography or magnetic resonance.
Detecting valve vegetations
Vegetations are sought on echocardiography, particularly the transoesophageal study.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 40

set2.io: Measure the cardiothoracic ratio to evaluate cardiac enlargement
set2.q: A properly performed posteroanterior chest radiograph shows the cardiac silhouette occupying 58 per cent of the internal thoracic diameter. What does that suggest?
opts: Cardiomegaly
Correct. The silhouette should normally occupy no more than about half the internal thoracic diameter, so this exceeds it.
A normal heart size
A normal ratio sits below about one half of the internal thoracic diameter, and this measurement is above it.
Pulmonary hypertension without cardiac enlargement
The ratio measures the cardiac silhouette rather than the pulmonary circulation.
A pericardial effusion specifically
An effusion can enlarge the silhouette, but the ratio identifies enlargement rather than its cause.
set2.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 8
